summary: Atlassian provides a developer console for creating OAuth 2.0 3LO apps. Developers must configure scopes, callback URLs, and register applications. Public distribution requires Atlassian approval, which involves a 10-15 business day review process and adherence to strict security guidelines.

steps.text: [OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps] Navigate to the developer console to create an app.

claim.text: Navigate to the developer console to create an app.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: From any page on developer.atlassian.com, select your profile icon in the top-right corner, and from the dropdown, select Developer console.

claim.text: Configure the OAuth 2.0 (3LO) settings.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Select Authorization in the left menu. Next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO), select Configure.

steps.text: [OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps] Add the required callback URL.

claim.text: Add the required callback URL.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Enter the Callback URL. Set this to any URL that is accessible by the app. When you implement OAuth 2.0 (3LO) in your app (see next section), the redirect_uri must match this URL.

steps.text: [OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps] Add APIs to the app.

claim.text: Add APIs to the app.
claim.label: official_docs

After creating the link, you should receive the OAuth credentials: Client ID and Client secret
